subject.title: Recipient-addressed outbound sends: resolve people through verified routes, not raw platform ids

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a core, cross-channel verified-recipient primitive for outbound sends, and should it be designed together with the raw-target guardrail and receipt work already tracked in the related open issues?
rationale: The request addresses a real cross-channel security boundary, but choosing the permanent core contract versus plugin-owned policy, the authoritative consent sources, and the relationship to existing outbound work cannot be resolved safely from source structure alone.

options.title: Sponsor a staged core design
options.body: Define recipient-route resolution and refusal semantics first, keep raw targets compatible, and coordinate its interfaces with the open raw-target and receipt proposals.

options.title: Limit core to a generic policy seam
options.body: Keep identity/consent registries plugin-owned and add only the smallest shared message-tool hook required for plugins to resolve or refuse recipients.

options.title: Defer pending existing outbound decisions
options.body: Resolve the raw-target gate and delivery-correlation direction first, then revisit whether a recipient registry remains necessary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged core design
recommendation.body: Define recipient-route resolution and refusal semantics first, keep raw targets compatible, and coordinate its interfaces with the open raw-target and receipt proposals.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses the shared message tool, gateway/outbound runtime, and security-sensitive agent behavior.
